name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean favors Democrats by default
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson is running for re-election with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Jackson at roughly 95 percent to win

model.rationale: The district's 18-point Democratic lean, Jackson's incumbency, and his roughly $418,000-to-$63,000 fundraising advantage over Christian Maxwell leave Maxwell with no evident path; markets price Jackson near 95 percent and the fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-to-high twenties.
model.watch: A dramatic national Republican wave or a late influx of outside spending against Jackson would be needed to put this race in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
This is a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat with an 18-point partisan lean. Incumbent Jonathan Jackson is running for re-election and holds a large financial advantage, having raised about $418,000 to Republican Christian Maxwell's $63,000. No public general-election polls are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets price Jackson's chances at roughly 95 percent.

The combination of a strong Democratic baseline, incumbency, and a wide money gap leaves Maxwell a very narrow path. Barring an extraordinary shift in the national environment or a sudden influx of outside spending, Jackson is positioned for a comfortable win in November. The main uncertainty is the exact size of the margin, which comparable elections suggest could fall anywhere from the mid-teens to around thirty points.
